title: fanoutqa: Identify the host cities of the Summer Olympic Games from 2000 to 2020 and name the main stadiums used in each of these Olympics. (c64872786e1a2ab6)

chat_history.content: Identify the host cities of the Summer Olympic Games from 2000 to 2020 and name the main stadiums used in each of these Olympics.

content.content:
We need list of host cities for Summer Olympics 2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020 and the main stadiums used. Provide answer. No need external lookup? I know:

2000 Sydney - Stadium: Stadium Australia (also known as ANZ Stadium)
2004 Athens - Olympic Stadium (Athens Olympic Stadium, also known as Spyros Louis)
2008 Beijing - Beijing National Stadium (Bird's Nest)
2012 London - Olympic Stadium (London) (now called London Stadium)
2016 Rio de Janeiro - Maracanã Stadium (Estádio do Maracanã) was main stadium for opening/closing ceremonies, athletics held at Estádio Olímpico João Havelange (also called Engenhão). Which is considered main? Usually "Main stadium" refers to the athletics and ceremonies stadium. For Rio, the main stadium was the Maracanã Stadium. However athletics were at the Olympic Stadium (Estádio Olímpico João Havelange). The "main stadium" could be the "Olympic Stadium". Wikipedia says "Main stadium: Estádio Olímpico João Havelange". The opening ceremony was at Maracanã. I'll provide both? But user asked name the main stadiums used in each of these Olympics. Provide the primary Olympic stadium where athletics took place, which is typical.

Thus:

2000 Sydney - Stadium Australia (ANZ Stadium)
2004 Athens - Olympic Stadium (Athens)
2008 Beijing - Beijing National Stadium (Bird's Nest)
2012 London - Olympic Stadium (London Stadium)
2016 Rio - Estádio Olímpico João Havelange (also known as Engenhão)
2020 Tokyo - Olympic Stadium (Japan National Stadium)

Note: 2020 Olympics held in 2021 due to COVID, main stadium is Japan National Stadium.

Provide in table format.

content:
**Summer Olympic Games 2000 – 2020 – Host cities and their main Olympic stadiums**

| Year | Host City (Country) | Main Olympic Stadium* | Notable facts |
|------|---------------------|-----------------------|----------------|
| 2000 | Sydney, Australia | **Stadium Australia** (also known as **ANZ Stadium**) | Built especially for the Games; hosted the opening/closing ceremonies and athletics. |
| 2004 | Athens, Greece | **Athens Olympic Stadium** (officially **Olympic Stadium “Spiros Louis”**) | Named after the first modern‑Olympic marathon winner; venue for athletics, ceremonies and the football final. |
| 2008 | Beijing, China | **Beijing National Stadium** (the **“Bird’s Nest”**) | Iconic lattice‑steel design; hosted athletics and both opening and closing ceremonies. |
| 2012 | London, United Kingdom | **London Olympic Stadium** (now the **London Stadium**) | Designed to be converted into a multi‑use venue after the Games; athletics and ceremonies were held here. |
| 2016 | Rio de Janeiro, Brazil | **Estádio Olímpico João Havelange** (commonly called **Engenhão**) | Primary athletics venue; the opening and closing ceremonies took place at the historic **Maracanã Stadium**, but the “main Olympic stadium” for competition was Engenhão. |
| 2020* | Tokyo, Japan | **Japan National Stadium** | A completely new, 68 000‑seat stadium rebuilt on the site of the 1964 Olympic venue; hosted athletics and the opening/closing ceremonies (the Games were held in 2021 due to the COVID‑19 pandemic). |

\*The 2020 Summer Olympics were postponed and actually took place from July 23 to August 8 2021, but they are officially still referred to as the “2020 Tokyo Olympics.”

**Key points**

* The “main Olympic stadium” usually refers to the venue that hosts the athletics competitions and the opening/closing ceremonies.  
* In Rio 2016, while the Maracanã Stadium was used for the ceremonies, the designated Olympic stadium for the sporting program was the Estádio Olímpico João Havelange.  
* All listed stadiums were either constructed especially for the Games or extensively renovated to meet Olympic standards.
